title: Why Save a History?
description: See why a shared project needs recoverable checkpoints before learning Git commands.

blocks.content: You and a teammate both edit the same proposal. You need to know what changed and recover a working version when an edit goes wrong. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

Version control keeps a history of saved project states. Git is a distributed version-control system: each local repository, a project folder plus its saved history, has its own copy. A commit is one saved checkpoint.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: A teammate overwrites a working paragraph. What does Git give you?
options: A history of saved project states
A way to avoid all conflicts
A single file with every version
blocks.explanation: Saved checkpoints let you inspect and recover earlier project states.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `stageFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
